newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Saudis see market strong enough to fit in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Saudis see market strong enough to fit in Iraq.

text.p: Influential OPEC members Saudi Arabia and Gulf allies producers say the oil market is strong enough to absorb additional Iraqi oil, should a U.N deal be implemented, A Gulf source said on Tuesday. However, the source said it remained to be seen just when a much-delayed Iraqi oil-for-food deal would be implemented.
The source said OPEC in June had already dealt with the possible resumption of Iraqi exports when it gave it a nominal quota of 1.2 million barrels per day (bpd).
"We gave them a quota already but you can't believe it (Iraq's return) until you see it," the source said.
The source said that demand for OPEC oil including stocks was obviously more than 26 million bpd.
Although OPEC has a quota of 25.03 million bpd, independent observers say the group is already producing about 26 million, even without Iraq.
"Demand is whatever OPEC is producing. We will definitely end this year with the lowest stocks in 20 years" the Gulf source said.
